report.source_text: Clinical examination revealed increased tone, hyperreflexia and reduced proprioception of the lower limbs. The patient also exhibited patchy paresthesia bilaterally to the level of the umbilicus. There was decreased anal tone on digital rectal examination. There was no clinical evidence of major head or spinal trauma and the remainder of his cranial nerve and general neurological examination was unremarkable. These findings were consistent with an upper motor neuron lesion.

report.source_text: Neurological symptoms improved shortly after completion of corticosteroid therapy. MRI whole spine was repeated on day 10, which showed almost complete resolution of the changes seen previously between T7 and T10. He regained full lower limb motor strength, the paresthesias completely resolved and the indwelling catheter was successfully removed. He was discharged to home on day 11 of admission.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute Transverse Myelitis (ATM) in the context of recent COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man with confirmed COVID-19 infection (PCR positive on day 7 of illness) presented with acute onset bilateral lower limb weakness, urinary retention, and constipation beginning 2 days after acute urinary retention. Neurological examination revealed increased tone, hyperreflexia, reduced proprioception in lower limbs, patchy paresthesia to the umbilical level bilaterally, and decreased anal tone—findings consistent with an upper motor neuron lesion. Spinal MRI demonstrated T2 signal elevation in the central spinal cord from T7 to T10 without enhancement or mass, confirming acute transverse myelitis. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated protein (0.79 g/L) with normal glucose (3.2 mmol/L), negative cultures, and negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR, supporting post-viral inflammatory myelitis. The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3 days and intensive physiotherapy. Neurological symptoms improved shortly after corticosteroid completion. Repeat spinal MRI on day 10 showed almost complete resolution of the T7-T10 signal abnormality. The patient regained full lower limb motor strength, paresthesias completely resolved, urinary catheter was successfully removed, and he was discharged to home on day 11 of admission.
